5479.title: Use blittable Byte for C bool and Int32 for hb_bool_t delegate callbacks
5479.body:
Use blittable Byte for C bool and Int32 for hb_bool_t delegate callbacks (#5479)

Context: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/136578
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5464
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5518

Match generated unmanaged callback delegates, function pointers, and
DelegateProxies implementations to their native C ABI boolean widths by using
1-byte Byte for Skia C/C++ bool and 4-byte Int32 for HarfBuzz hb_bool_t, while
keeping public managed delegate and API signatures on bool.

~~ Use 1-byte Byte for Skia C/C++ bool callbacks ~~

SkiaSharpGenerator mapped C bool to Byte for struct fields, but overrode
callback parameters and returns back to bool with [MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.I1)].
[UnmanagedCallersOnly] and delegate* unmanaged[Cdecl] ignore [MarshalAs], and
the Mono ARM64 interpreter (dotnet/runtime#136578) does not zero-extend bool
returns across the 32-bit return register expected by Apple ARM64 C++ callers.

Map C bool to Byte in GetManagedFunctionArguments and GetFunctionPointerType
(BaseTool.cs), remove [return: MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.I1)] from WriteDelegate
and WriteDelegateProxy (Generator.cs), and update the Skia stream, write-stream,
and Graphite image-provider proxy implementations to convert between byte and
bool. Forward P/Invoke declarations in WriteFunctions keep
[MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.I1)] bool.

~~ Use 4-byte Int32 for HarfBuzz hb_bool_t callbacks ~~

HarfBuzz defines typedef int hb_bool_t; (4 bytes), which libHarfBuzzSharp.json
maps to "Boolean". Treating "Boolean" the same as C bool generated 1-byte I1 or
unmarshaled bool returns instead of 4-byte int callbacks.

Map "Boolean" to Int32 for callback delegates and function pointers, update the
HarfBuzz font and Unicode proxy implementations to return 1 or 0, and return 0
immediately in FontGetGlyphNameProxyImplementation before copying the name span
when GlyphNameDelegate returns false. HBFontFuncsTest and HBUnicodeFuncsTest
verify false-returning callbacks.

5475.title: [tests] Make post-GC and post-dispose HandleDictionary test assertions address-reuse safe
5475.body:
[tests] Make HandleDictionary assertions address-reuse safe (#5475)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5464
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4080
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1653003
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1653279
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1655413

Verify post-dispose and post-GC wrapper teardown by wrapper reference and
registration-token identity in HandleDictionary.instances instead of querying
SKObject.GetInstance<TDerived>(handle, out _) after native memory is freed.
This prevents parallel xUnit tests that reuse a freed native pointer from
causing false failures while catching disposed or collected wrappers whose
dictionary entries were not removed.

~~ Inspect HandleDictionary.instances by wrapper and token identity ~~

During parallel xUnit runs of SkiaSharp.Tests, tests that freed a native object
via Dispose() or CollectGarbage() and then asserted
Assert.False(SKObject.GetInstance<TDerived>(handle, out _)) intermittently
failed when another test thread allocated a new native object at the same
address (malloc ABA reuse). Under THROW_OBJECT_EXCEPTIONS in Debug builds,
HandleDictionary.GetInstanceNoLocks<TDerived> throws InvalidOperationException
("A managed object exists for the handle, but is not the expected type") when a
live owning wrapper of a different concrete type occupies the reused handle,
such as an SKImage at a freed SKTypeface address or an SKDynamicMemoryWStream
at a freed SKMemoryStream address. When a parallel test allocated the same
wrapper type at that address, GetInstance<TDerived> returned true and failed
Assert.False.

Calling HandleDictionary.GetInstance<SKObject> also missed real teardown bugs.
GetInstanceNoLocks filters out wrappers with IsDisposed == true and ignores
dead WeakReference entries, so the existing AssertDeregistered helper from
#4080 could not detect a disposed wrapper left in HandleDictionary.instances.
In addition, SKCodec and SKDocument implement ISKSkipObjectRegistration, so
GetInstance<SKCodec> and GetInstance<SKDocument> always returned false without
checking whether those wrappers were collected.

Update AssertDeregistered<TSkiaObject>(IntPtr handle, TSkiaObject instance) and
add Track(SKObject instance, out IntPtr handle, out WeakReference weak) and
AssertCollected(IntPtr handle, WeakReference instance) in
SKHandleDictionaryTestHelpers:

  * AssertDeregistered asserts handle != IntPtr.Zero, instance != null,
    instance.IsDisposed, and instance.Handle == IntPtr.Zero (which is zeroed by
    SKObject.Handle after DeregisterHandle), then reads
    HandleDictionary.instances under instancesLock and asserts
    !ReferenceEquals(current.Target, instance). Update 8 post-dispose assertions
    in SKCodecTest, SKTypefaceTest, SKManagedStreamTest, and
    SKRuntimeEffectTest to call AssertDeregistered.
  * Track captures handle = instance.Handle while the wrapper is live and
    asserts handle != IntPtr.Zero. For ISKSkipObjectRegistration types
    (SKCodec and SKDocument), it allocates a fresh WeakReference(instance); for
    registered types, it reads HandleDictionary.instances under instancesLock
    and asserts that the handle maps to instance, returning that exact
    WeakReference registration entry.
  * AssertCollected requires instance.Target is null (rejecting a wrapper that
    is still strongly reachable even if IsDisposed is true) and reads
    HandleDictionary.instances under instancesLock to assert
    !ReferenceEquals(current, instance). Because RegisterHandle allocates a new
    WeakReference on every registration, a concurrent test reusing the freed
    pointer installs a distinct WeakReference instance, whereas an unremoved
    dead entry from the original registration fails the assertion. Update 13
    post-GC tests across SKCodecTest, SKDocumentTest, SKFontManagerTest,
    SKImageTest, SKManagedStreamTest, SKManagedWStreamTest, and SKTypefaceTest
    to use Track and AssertCollected.

~~ Preserve owner liveness and helper-frame boundaries across GC checks ~~

In SKCodecTest.StreamLosesOwnershipAndCanBeGarbageCollected,
SKTypefaceTest.StreamLosesOwnershipAndCanBeGarbageCollected,
SKManagedStreamTest.StreamLosesOwnershipAndCanBeGarbageCollected, and
SKManagedWStreamTest.StreamIsReferencedAndNotDisposedPrematurely, DoWork runs
an inner CollectGarbage(), uses the owner (codec.GetPixels,
typeface.GetTableTags, or document.BeginPage/EndPage/Close), and then asserts
Assert.True(SKObject.GetInstance<...>(streamHandle, out var stream)) to verify
that OwnedObjects or KeepAliveObjects retained the child stream. Without a
subsequent reference to the owner, the JIT could treat codec, typeface, or
document as dead after its last native call and finalize it before the inner
GetInstance assertion ran. Add GC.KeepAlive on the owning wrapper at the end of
DoWork so it remains live through the inner retention check and becomes
collectible only after DoWork returns, and mark all 17 local allocation/work
helpers across the 7 post-GC test files with
[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)] so JIT inlining cannot extend local
lifetimes into the outer test frame.

In SKTypefaceTest.ManagedStreamIsCollectedWhenCollected,
SKTypeface.FromStream(SKStreamAsset) calls SKFontManager.CreateTypeface, which
copies an SKManagedStream via managed.ToMemoryStream() and immediately calls
managed.Dispose(), zeroing stream.Handle. The base test read stream.Handle
after FromStream returned, passing IntPtr.Zero to GetInstance<SKManagedStream>
and never tracking the created SKTypeface. When stream was tracked before
FromStream inside DoWork in build 1653003, Android (API 21) Tests and Android
(API 36) Tests failed with "Expected SKManagedStream (handle 0x...) to be
garbage-collected, but it is still reachable" because Mono's conservative stack
scanner retained the dead local slot in DoWork's frame.

  * Move SKManagedStream creation and Track(stream, ...) into a nested
    [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining)] static CreateTypeface helper
    before SKTypeface.FromStream(stream), then track typeface, call
    CollectGarbage(), assert Assert.NotEmpty(typeface.GetTableTags()), and keep
    typeface alive in DoWork. Executing CollectGarbage() and GetTableTags()
    after CreateTypeface returns overwrites the inner stack frame before the
    outer collection check, and tracking both stream and typeface verifies that
    both wrappers are collected and dotnet.Position throws
    ObjectDisposedException.

~~ Drain queued finalizers asynchronously for non-skipped Mono and WASM tests ~~

Eleven of the thirteen post-GC tests call SkipOnMono(), which skips on Android,
iOS, Mac Catalyst, and Browser WASM. The remaining two tests —
SKDocumentTest.StreamIsNotCollectedPrematurely and
SKTypefaceTest.ManagedStreamIsCollectedWhenCollected — run on all platforms. In
build 1653003, both failed on WASM Tests and WASM (.NET Preview) Tests with
"Collected wrapper is still registered under handle 0x588dd08" and "0x5153608".
On single-threaded Browser WASM, synchronous BaseTest.CollectGarbage() clears
the short WeakReference.Target to null, but ~SKNativeObject() does not run
DeregisterHandle until execution yields to the runtime event loop.

Add CollectGarbageAndAssertCollectedAsync(IntPtr handle, WeakReference instance)
in SKHandleDictionaryTestHelpers and use it in those two tests. It polls
BaseTest.CollectGarbage() inside await AssertEx.Eventually(..., timeout: 5000),
yielding via Task.Delay between attempts until instance.Target is null and
HandleDictionary.instances no longer holds ReferenceEquals(current, instance),
then falls through to AssertCollected(handle, instance) so any timeout reports
whether the wrapper stayed reachable or its registration token remained in the
dictionary. Keeping AssertCollected strict avoids a Mono/WASM platform branch
that would accept IsDisposed targets or dead !current.IsAlive entries and mask
rooting leaks or broken finalizer deregistration.

All 38 SkiaSharp.Tests runs in Azure Pipelines builds 1653279 and 1655413
passed with zero failures across Linux, macOS, Windows (.NET Core and .NET
Framework x86/x64), Android (API 21 and API 36), iOS, Mac Catalyst, WASM
(1,160 passed, 112 skipped), and WASM (.NET Preview) (1,160 passed, 112
skipped), and the local macOS ARM64 .NET 10 console suite passed (6,473 passed,
23 skipped in SkiaSharp.Tests.dll, plus 1 SingletonInit, 50 Gallery, 4 Vulkan,
and 2 Direct3D tests).

5506.title: Fix StringUtilities.GetUnicodeCharacterCode and GetString validation
5506.body:
Fix StringUtilities.GetUnicodeCharacterCode and GetString validation (#5506)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5446
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1654542

Validate and decode single-unit character codes in StringUtilities by encoded
byte width rather than UTF-16 string length, and guard null byte arrays before
dereferencing Length in StringUtilities.GetString.

~~ Validate and decode single-unit character codes by byte width ~~

Fuzzing StringUtilities with the managed-parsers target in #5446 threw an
unexpected ArgumentException from BitConverter.ToInt32 whenever
GetUnicodeCharacterCode was called with SKTextEncoding.Utf8 or
SKTextEncoding.Utf16. GetUnicodeStringLength required character.Length == 1 for
both encodings, but a single UTF-16 char encodes to 1-3 bytes in UTF-8 and 2
bytes in UTF-16, which is always shorter than the 4 bytes required by
BitConverter.ToInt32(bytes, 0). For SKTextEncoding.Utf32, GetUnicodeStringLength
required character.Length == 2, rejecting 1-char BMP strings such as "A" that
encode to a single 4-byte UTF-32 unit while accepting 2-char BMP strings such as
"AB", encoding them to 8 bytes, and returning only the first character's code.

Character-code consumers such as SKFontManager.MatchCharacter(int),
SKFont.GetGlyph(int), and SKTypeface.GetGlyph(int) expect a Unicode code point
(SkUnichar). A character's little-endian encoded bytes equal its code point only
when the character fits in one code unit of the requested encoding: 1 byte for
Utf8 (U+0000..U+007F), 2 bytes for Utf16 (U+0000..U+FFFF), and 4 bytes for Utf32
(U+0000..U+10FFFF). Remove GetUnicodeStringLength, require bytes.Length to match
encoding.GetCharacterByteSize(), and decode 1, 2, or 4 bytes via bytes[0],
BitConverter.ToUInt16(bytes, 0), or BitConverter.ToInt32(bytes, 0).

  * Pass the message first and nameof(character) second to ArgumentException
    when bytes.Length != encoding.GetCharacterByteSize(). The previous call
    reversed (message, paramName), reporting "character" as the message and
    "Only a single character can be specified." as ParamName.

StringUtilitiesTest covers expected code points for "A" (Utf8, Utf16, Utf32),
"ä" and "年" (Utf16, Utf32), and "🚀" (Utf32), along with ArgumentNullException on
null, ArgumentException on empty, multi-character, or multi-unit inputs with
ParamName == "character", and ArgumentOutOfRangeException on GlyphId and
out-of-range SKTextEncoding values.

~~ Guard null byte arrays before reading Length in GetString ~~

StringUtilities.GetString(byte[], SKTextEncoding) forwarded to
GetString(data, 0, data.Length, encoding), dereferencing data.Length before
reaching the null check in the 4-parameter overload and throwing
NullReferenceException instead of ArgumentNullException when data was null.

Check data == null and throw ArgumentNullException(nameof(data)) before reading
data.Length so both byte[] overloads report the same exception and parameter
name. StringUtilitiesTest verifies both overloads across Utf8, Utf16, and Utf32,
and the .NET 10 console test suite and Azure Pipelines build 1654542 passed.

5477.title: Clarify release audits with shipment, branch readiness and sync tables
5477.body:
Release: separate audit shipment, readiness, and sync views (#5477)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/40789226474

The release audit now keeps shipment, Prepare-base readiness, and upstream sync
work in separate views so each recommended action is accompanied by evidence
from the ref to which it applies. This makes pending release work actionable
without allowing CI or status from a different branch to imply readiness.

~~ Preserve release-stage evidence boundaries ~~

Render current releases, branch readiness, and upstream/sync work as distinct
tables. The release view pairs public shipments and an unpublished cut with its
own exact-cut build/BAR and release action; the readiness view reports the
maintenance or main base, its additional commits, its exact-base build/BAR, and
its readiness action; the sync view reports its comparison base, incoming PR,
exact-sync-source build, and sync action.

Keep detail such as full SHA and BAR evidence below the applicable table, retain
finished history in JSON, and preserve the existing release action gates and
exit-code meanings. This prevents a green base build from being presented as a
failed release branch's publication evidence, and keeps future sync work from
becoming a release-table action.

~~ Make pending branch work visible ~~

Collect open PRs for the selected maintenance and release-cut targets, paging
through the GitHub results, and include them as `openPullRequests` in JSON.
Display that work below the compact branch-readiness table, including at the
80- and 120-column render widths covered by the publishing regression tests.

Open PRs remain separate from merged commits and are presented for inclusion
review rather than being treated as automatic release blockers.

~~ Tie sync CI to the incoming source ~~

When an incoming sync PR supplies a head branch and SHA, collect package-build
evidence for that exact source and reject conflicting audited commits for the
same branch. The sync table uses this source build rather than maintenance or
prepared-cut CI, then emits its full build detail so newer failed or canceled
reruns remain visible after a usable succeeded BAR build.

The publishing regression suite covers release/base CI isolation, open-PR
filtering and visibility, numeric shipment selection, and sync rerun
diagnostics. The head's Release - Tooling Tests run completed successfully.

5434.title: [tests] Use the Android CLI for provisioning and device lifecycle
5434.body:
[tests] Use the Android CLI for provisioning and device lifecycle (#5434)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5373
Context: b5db2e3c09d3520dff2b67b11013fe9a7cbd6d07
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1650591
Context: https://github.com/Redth/AndroidSdk.Tools/pull/94
Context: https://github.com/Redth/AndroidSdk.Tools/pull/95

Make the released dotnet android tool responsible for SDK provisioning and
emulator readiness, with one ordinary device-test lifecycle shared by local
and CI runs. Keep direct consumer-side emulator control limited to
exact-serial shutdown and the additional disposable-CI emulator reset.

Carry forward the reusable Android foundation from #5373 without its Appium
server/APK preparation, sample jobs or mobile scenarios. Appium callers must
retain TEST_ANDROID_PREINSTALL_APPIUM_SERVER and InstallAndroidAppiumArtifacts
above this layer, including their conditional CPU/memory settings and
preinstalled marker. The legacy integration-test tree remains unchanged.

~~ Provision through one selected SDK ~~

Update AndroidSdk.Tool from 0.35.1 to 0.36.0 and restore repository tools before
Android provisioning and pre-build hooks. Preserve the existing non-container
build-step restore scope and also cover managed Android provisioning when
that normal build-step path is disabled.

Replace Get-AndroidSdk, Get-SdkManager and Get-Adb, manual command-line-tools
archive handling, and sdkmanager invocations fed by yes.txt with the CLI's
sdk find/info/download/install commands. Select InstallDestination first,
then ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, ANDROID_HOME, CLI discovery and finally the user's
android-sdk directory. Download command-line tools when HasCmdlineTools is
false, and export the selected absolute path as ANDROID_HOME,
ANDROID_SDK_ROOT and AndroidSdkDirectory. Stop exporting
ANDROID_SDK_MANAGER_PATH and ANDROID_ADB_PATH; consumers no longer need those
executable-discovery results.

Accept a deduplicated package array and pass repeated --package arguments to
one install command. Translate the comma-separated API list into platform
packages through that same helper. The bootstrapper requests platform-tools
and build-tools 35.0.0/36.0.0 together instead of separate SDK/tool steps.
The tool manifest and three provisioning scripts are byte-identical to the
referenced extraction source. SDK setup and the Release Android device-host
build also passed with the selected local SDK.

~~ Delegate readiness instead of owning emulator processes ~~

Replace AndroidAvdCommand and AndroidAvdWindowsArguments with CLI AVD
create/start/delete. Remove ANDROID_EMULATOR_PROCESS and its redirected-output
tasks: the consumer no longer retains the native launcher or implements
WaitForAndroidBoot, AssertOwnedAndroidEmulator and
AndroidEmulatorIdentityLines. Readiness, SDK/image checks and animation
configuration now live in the tool rather than another SDK-process, identity
or polling layer.

Retain the unique AVD name, unused even console/transport port pair in
5554..5682, x64-to-x86_64/ARM64-to-arm64-v8a mapping, default
android-36;google_apis image and Nexus 5X model. Start with
--wait --timeout 300 --no-animations, CPU threshold 3 and response threshold 5;
use swiftshader_indirect on Linux and guest elsewhere. Keep the headless,
no-snapshot/audio/boot-animation options, 4096 partition and disabled cameras.
The CLI owns the readiness deadline; Cake adds no second process timeout.
Physical mode acquires no AVD.

Use the same caller-owned teardown after startup or test failure in both
modes. Dump properties, send one adb -s <serial> emu kill, then perform normal
AVD deletion. Clear ownership after those commands return successfully, and
aggregate a cleanup error after the original operation error when both exist.
The direct ADB stop is a compatibility seam: 0.36.0 has no avd stop command.
It deliberately does not re-identify the guest, poll disappearance or verify
native shutdown before deleting metadata; strict local pre-ADB recovery is
not provided by this implementation.

The pinned CLI also has a known exit-status limitation: Program.Main discards
app.Run(args), so checking process exits cannot establish that every handler
succeeded. The correction in Redth/AndroidSdk.Tools#94 and strict lifecycle
work in Redth/AndroidSdk.Tools#95 are upstream context, not dependencies
consumed by this pin. Do not mistake this change for a fix to those contracts.

A real macOS ARM64/API36 lifecycle passed 24 assertions, including exact
serial/API/ABI, all three disabled animation settings, owned metadata removal
and unchanged inventory in that probe. The unfiltered .NET 10 console solution
passed 6,503 tests with 47 existing skips using --parallel none. No product
ownership code or test/skip policy changes accompany this infrastructure work.

~~ Keep deployment and execution on the selected serial ~~

DeviceRunnersDevice selected the test runner's device, but did not supply the
Android SDK's deployment target. Pass the retained serial through both
DeviceRunnersDevice and AdbTarget="-s <serial>", so bundletool APK generation
and installation use the same device as test execution. Do not rediscover a
device between those phases.

Remove ListAndroidDevices and its informational startup inventories; the
retained serial, not inventory order or an inferred default, selects the
emulator. Physical mode continues without an acquired serial override.

The actual Android Cake entry point completed Release pre-build, API36 boot,
application deployment, execution and teardown in 7m01.65s: 1,201 passed,
83 existing skips and zero failures. DeviceRunners selected emulator-5554 and
the production teardown deleted that run's AVD. This is application-execution
evidence, not merely a successful startup probe or a cross-platform guarantee.

~~ Prevent failed CI attempts from contaminating retries ~~

Build 1650591 ran API21 successfully with 1,191 passed and 93 skips, then its
teardown refused the guest identity before stop/delete. The mismatching value
was not captured, so its cause cannot be attributed to casing, whitespace or
a particular property. The automatic retry started emulator-5556 while
emulator-5554 remained alive. DeviceRunners then failed during logcat setup:
"More than one Device/Emulator detected", despite explicit serial routing.
Selecting a serial alone therefore did not prevent that retry failure.

On disposable CI agents, StopCIAndroidEmulators terminates processes named
emulator or prefixed qemu-system- by PID, including their process trees.
Run it before pre-build and again in the stop helper's finally, including
when setup acquired no AVD or diagnostics/owned shutdown throws. Keep local
and CI create/start/property/stop/delete behavior otherwise identical:
BuildSystem.IsLocalBuild belongs only in this extra CI reset helper.
Listing/dry-run invocations must not terminate emulator processes.

Wait up to 30 seconds after each CI kill, but warn and continue if the process
has not exited; slow shutdown alone must not discard an otherwise passing
job. Actual process inspection/kill errors still propagate. This is
deliberately coarse disposable-agent cleanup, not exact-owner local recovery.

Fixture-PID tests passed seven process cases, including unrelated-process
preservation and the warning-only wait branch. Seven production Cake-hook
assertions verified entry-before-build cleanup and teardown after an injected
setup failure without AVD acquisition. Local and simulated-CI command traces
also matched, with 47 assertions passing in each mode.

~~ Retain raw CLI diagnostics after successful runs ~~

A cleanup refusal without the actual property value is insufficient to
diagnose old guests. Keep one logged RunAndroidCli(FilePath, params string[])
boundary for create, start, property inspection and delete. It quotes
arguments, passes the selected ANDROID_HOME as --home, uses the repository
working directory, creates the log parent with Cake path/directory APIs and
sets ANDROID_TOOL_PROCESS_RUNNER_LOG_PATH. There is no unlogged overload.

Write android-create.log, android-start.log and android-delete.log beneath
output/logs/testlogs/android/<AVD>/, and the unparsed property dump beneath
output/logs/testlogs/android-cleanup/<AVD>/android-cleanup.log. Filter the
property command by the anchored owned serial. JSON console output trims
property values and cannot replace the raw subprocess evidence.

Review identified that a log under output/logs/android would be lost on
successful device jobs: their existing always-published artifact contains
output/logs/testlogs. Put the logs inside that retained tree rather than
broadening artifact publication. The real application run produced nonempty
create/start/delete logs and an 80,907-byte raw property log. Runner probes
also verified nested directory creation and an SDK path containing spaces.

5489.title: [skia-sync] Merge upstream chrome/m156 bug fixes
5489.body:
Sync Skia M156 compiler fixes (#5489)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/411
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5491
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/40753002638
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/4ad087ae366e7e7a2b0028ba760d3c3618ce8bf7...bb94f003e3884a00f0fbd824edc344ce66f7b7b3

Adopt two upstream chrome/m156 SkSL fixes without changing the product
milestone, package versions, managed API, or native ABI.

~~ Reject Raster Pipeline slot-count overflow ~~

Large shader programs could overflow value-slot counts, individual temporary
stack depths, or the sum of those depths. The upstream fix checks allocation
and stack arithmetic, avoids overflowing peephole instruction coalescing, and
rejects invalid counts before allocating slot storage.

Native regressions cover value-slot wraparound past 2^32, single-stack depth
overflow, and aggregate temporary-stack overflow.

~~ Reject invalid runtime-effect types during parsing ~~

Reserved types such as sampler2D and texture2D alias the invalid type in
runtime effects. Reject them in Parser::type so struct members and other type
uses receive an error before later validation. Remove the duplicate
variable-declaration diagnostic and update the affected error baselines.

The upstream regression declares invalid sampler2D and texture2D struct
members and expects both to be rejected.

~~ Record the merged native identity without changing the reviewed tree ~~

Advance externals/skia and the governance fork hash together to
bb94f003e3884a00f0fbd824edc344ce66f7b7b3, the actual mono/skia merge commit.
Keep upstream_merge_commit at 961c7e83d9434470c588f210a1bb5375f2970d73,
the exact chrome/m156 revision integrated by the native PR.

The native merge contains reviewed commit f42a4291d12381a9f770c4fe064d511cd642a819
as a direct parent and has an identical tree. Preserve that merge ancestry
rather than squashing or rebasing the upstream history. The dependent repin
changes only the gitlink and governance fork hash.

5377.title: Build SkiaSharp.Views.Uno.WinUI against Uno Platform 7
5377.body:
Build SkiaSharp.Views.Uno.WinUI against Uno Platform 7 (#5377)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/5174
Context: https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/pull/24260

Rebuild the Uno views package and samples around Uno Platform 7's unified
renderer and .NET 10 baseline. Replace the obsolete per-platform runtime
packaging with one common Uno implementation, preserve existing control usage
with a CPU fallback where Uno exposes no swap chain, and keep generated samples
on the same managed and native product cohort.

~~ Rebuild the package for the Uno 7 assembly model ~~

The base package referenced Uno.WinUI 5.2.175 and the `Uno` and
`Uno.UI.Toolkit` assemblies. Uno 7 renamed those assemblies to `Uno.WinRT` and
`Uno.UI.Extras` without forwarders, so startup failed while initializing
`SkiaSharp.Views.Windows.GlobalStaticResources` before `OnLaunched` ran.

Build the common implementation against Uno.WinUI 7.0.0-dev.2333 and require
net10.0 for the non-Windows assembly. Keep the existing Windows TFMs as package
facades over `SkiaSharp.Views.WinUI`. Remove the Android, iOS, macOS, and
Mac Catalyst platform implementations, plus the separate Skia and WASM runtime
projects, their `uno-runtime` packaging, and the WASM JavaScript bridge. Uno 7
no longer selects those native-renderer variants, and Uno.Sdk now supplies the
platform native assets.

Move the applications to Uno.Sdk 7.0.0-dev.79, its `Skia` feature name, and its
Android `UnoPlatformHost` startup model. Use Uno.Monaco.Editor 7.0.0-dev.3 for
SkiaFiddle. Remove the Basic sample's WASM splash workaround because the merged
upstream fix requests a record and raises the frame notification used to remove
the loader.

~~ Preserve SKSwapChainPanel compatibility without a swap chain ~~

Non-Windows Uno targets no longer expose the swap chain or GPU context used by
the former platform implementations. Make `SKSwapChainPanel` a `Grid` that
hosts `SKXamlCanvas`, reports a null `GRContext`, and raises `PaintSurface` with
the raster surface plus a size-and-format `GRBackendRenderTarget` whose
framebuffer is zero. `SKCanvasElement` remains the GPU-backed choice on Uno;
the WinAppSDK facade continues to use the ANGLE-backed Windows control.

The Uno control now derives from `Grid` instead of `FrameworkElement` and drops
`RaiseOnUnsupported`, which only controlled the previous unsupported-platform
exception. `DrawInBackground` remains unsupported. `EnableRenderLoop` attaches
to `CompositionTarget.Rendering` only while the control is loaded and visible.

Review found re-entry and unload-lifetime hazards in the replacement redraw
path. Keep `Invalidate()` deferred and coalesced so a handler cannot
synchronously re-enter `PaintSurface`, and discard canvas redraws that execute
after the final unload. The latter guard runs before bitmap allocation,
preventing detached work from creating a pinned pixel buffer that no later
unload would release. A subsequent load invalidates again, so reattached
controls still redraw.

~~ Keep generated samples on one product cohort ~~

Uno.Sdk 7 brings HarfBuzzSharp native assets at its own stable version, while
generated samples restore only the staged PR artifact cohort. Add an
unconditional `HarfBuzzSharpVersion` override beside `SkiaSharpVersion`, teach
the sample generator to stamp both product versions, and verify both packages
exist in the generated artifact set. This prevents the previous NU1103 restore
failure.

The generator removes `_UnoPlatformSamples.targets`, so SkiaFiddle previously
had no managed product reference after generation: its native assets could be
stamped at the current version while normal feeds could select an older
managed SkiaSharp. Add direct SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp project references
so the generator emits matching managed package references. Explicitly
reference the Uno views from Gallery because Uno.Sdk 7 no longer supplies
them, while keeping the generated WinUI package reference out of the in-tree
build to avoid a duplicate SDK reference.

~~ Retire the WasmShell native-asset path ~~

Remove the `IsUnoHead` and `UnoRuntimeIdentifier=WebAssembly` branches that fed
static libraries and `WasmShell*` linker items to Uno.Wasm.Bootstrap's former
emcc pipeline. Uno 7 builds WASM through the .NET SDK, which continues to use
the existing `UsingMicrosoftNETSdkWebAssembly` path for SkiaSharp and
HarfBuzzSharp native assets.

Delete `utils/NativeLibraryMiniTest/wasm`, its Uno.Wasm.Bootstrap 2.1 project,
and its bootstrap page. Nothing invoked that utility, while the maintained Uno
samples and browser sample tests exercise the .NET SDK WebAssembly integration.
This intentionally ends compatibility with pre-Uno 7 WasmShell pipelines.

~~ Make the samples usable on phone-sized targets ~~

Uno 7's Android heads render edge to edge, so apply visible-bounds padding on
all sides instead of leaving the Basic drawing toolbar under the navigation bar
and the Gallery header under the status bar. Below 720 pixels, move the
Gallery's controls below the canvas and collapse them vertically so the fixed
290-pixel sidebar does not consume most of a phone-width layout.

Subscribe to Android `BackRequested` only while a sample page is active. Any
subscriber makes Uno consume the native back callback, even when the handler
does not mark it handled, so retaining the subscription on the Gallery root
prevented system back from leaving the application. Use `SKCanvasElement` for
the GPU sample on Uno targets and retain `SKSwapChainPanel` for WinAppSDK.

~~ Keep browser validation strict under Uno 7 ~~

Uno.Wasm.Bootstrap probes the HTTP cache with `only-if-cached`; Chromium reports
a handled miss as the exact console error
`Failed to load resource: net::ERR_CACHE_MISS`. Ignore only that message while
continuing to fail browser tests for other console errors.

Refresh the drawn and cleared Uno references for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Uno 7 shifted rounded-control antialiasing and the tab indicator enough to
produce about 0.125% differing pixels against the existing 0.075% comparison
budget. The references now capture the settled Uno 7 output without relaxing
comparison policy.

Azure build 1651574 and the current-head GitHub checks passed, including managed
and native builds, NuGet packaging, WASM tests, and sample build and host jobs.

~~ Remove unsupported compatibility branches ~~

Drop `WINDOWS_UWP`, `UAP10_0_10240`, and `NETSTANDARD1_3` conditionals from the
shared binding code. Remove `HAS_UNO`, `HAS_UNO_WINUI`, UWP-namespace, and Uno
visibility branches that existed to compile shared Android, iOS, and macOS
views into the deleted native-renderer projects. The active Android, Apple,
Blazor, Windows, and current managed branches remain in their owning projects.

Remove the deleted runtime projects from solution filters and update package and
.NET-version guidance to describe the Uno 7 package shape, CPU fallback, and
Uno.Sdk-owned WASM native assets.

[tests] Stabilize golden capture retries and Uno drawing test (#5433)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5373

Keep strict screenshot comparison while distinguishing a first observed mismatch
from the deadline that governs later retries. This extracts and completes the
golden-retry and Uno-settling work carried from #5373 without changing reviewed
reference images or comparison tolerance.

~~ Preserve mismatch diagnostics after a consumed deadline ~~

A first capture can complete after its nominal deadline has been consumed and
still produce the only useful mismatch diagnostic. `Golden.RetryAsync` now takes
one immediate confirmation capture after that first mismatch, giving it the
shared five-second default capture budget. If the confirmation does not match,
later retries still use the original elapsed-clock deadline rather than renewing
it; a persistent mismatch is reported instead of being replaced by a timeout.
The asynchronous post-deadline regression exercises that confirmation path.

Both `VerifyAsync` forms now order optional arguments as `options`, `timeout`,
`retryInterval`, and `cancellationToken`. Null defaults select five seconds and
100 milliseconds respectively, and the cadence regression verifies the requested
interval for resolved and direct comparisons. Callers and guidance use named
arguments, so removing `SampleImage.DefaultTimeout` does not retain its former
two-second policy implicitly.

  * Rename golden-store lookup diagnostics from `Attempts` to `CandidateKeys`
    so they cannot be confused with capture retries, and remove the unused
    `FormatMarker` surface while retaining marker emission inside verification.
  * Document the Golden public surface and update the golden-image examples to
    reflect the named asynchronous arguments.

~~ Recover the Uno drawing interaction without relaxing verification ~~

The Uno drawing browser test now verifies its drawn state through the shared
Golden retry path with a ten-second budget and one-second interval. A missed
initial colour-swatch interaction can otherwise leave the expected strokes
absent even though the canvas has loaded. On a failed drawn comparison, the test
performs at most two complete clear-and-redraw recoveries, verifies the cleared
reference before retrying, and increments brush size only on the first attempt
because Clear retains that setting. The strict drawn and cleared references
remain the acceptance criteria.

[Build] Modernize Windows builds with VS 2026 and ANGLE chromium/8118 (#5321)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5325

Modernize Windows native, WinUI, and ANGLE builds around Visual Studio 2026,
MSVC v145, and Windows SDK 10.0.28000.0. Incorporate the final work from the
superseded ANGLE draft while retaining a single owning change. This does not
alter managed public APIs or the Skia C API; the WinUI project's declared
minimum remains Windows 10 build 17763.

~~ Make Windows tool selection and provisioning consistent ~~

Replace the previous mix of standalone SDK, LLVM, Ninja, and legacy toolset
provisioning with separate selection and component-installation steps for an

profile change invalidates Windows-native cache entries.

LLVM, Ninja, and architecture-specific Spectre library directory consistently.
The shared preflight rejects an absent VS install or SDK; toolset selection
requires MSVC 14.50 or later, and the Spectre lookup fails with the selected
path when its matching libraries are missing. This addresses source benchmarks
that could select an MSVC toolset without its corresponding Spectre libraries.

    guidance to VS 2026. Public jobs obtain Python through UsePythonVersion,
    whereas internal 1ES Windows jobs use their image-provided executable;

cannot alter the build. Update Component Governance entries for ANGLE and the

selected Visual Studio LLVM installation. Chromium resource tooling receives a

the resource compiler download is checked against its declared SHA-1. Retain
only the required ANGLE submodules, restore the SPIR-V inputs required by the
translator, and disable unneeded Rust, Siso, test, Vulkan-system-info, and
Vulkan backend paths.

process local Microsoft IDL imports, and fail for missing metadata, imports,
headers, or midlrt failures. This replaces the previous stub-header fallback,
which could allow an unresolved ABI dependency to reach the ANGLE compile.

package those PDBs with the corresponding DLLs. Extend Windows symbol validation
to compare each WindowsSymbols artifact basename with the DLL's embedded CodeView

whose PDB GUID and age are valid but whose embedded filename no longer identifies
the shipped PDB.

entry points. Inspection commands and non-Windows aggregate targets can now load
the scripts without synthetic VS/LLVM paths, while Windows builds still validate

5422.title: [tests] Unify golden-image tests across visual and sample suites
5422.body:
[tests] Unify golden-image tests across visual and sample suites (#5422)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5413
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5421

Give visual and non-Appium sample tests one catalog-free golden identity,
resolution, comparison, and diagnostic model. Keep reference discovery explicit,
preserve each consumer's rendering and comparison policy, and make captures
reviewable without introducing schemas, compatibility layers, or shared image
byte caches.

~~ Share one golden identity and verification model ~~

Visual tests previously used GoldenStore, GoldenTolerance, and VisualPlatform,
while sample tests maintained SampleImageOptions, Expected paths, and a
source-linked pixel comparer. Those parallel paths made lookup, retries,
attachments, and failure traces evolve independently.

Replace them with five shared responsibilities: GoldenCase validates identity
and orders candidates, GoldenStore indexes consumer-supplied disk or resource
sources, GoldenInput describes paths, encoded bytes, pixels, or retryable
captures, GoldenOptions carries comparison policy, and Golden performs the
verification. Stores cache source metadata but read the selected bytes for each
verification, so updated references are not hidden by a process-wide byte cache.

An omitted version selects the profile root. For a requested version, select the
lowest version directory greater than or equal to it, making each directory an
inclusive upper-bound snapshot. Functional variants precede architecture, named
variants never borrow siblings, and architecture may fall back only within the
same variant. Profile fallback is explicit:
`nanoserver -> windows -> portable`; other non-portable profiles may use
`portable`.

Keep the established visual raster, visual GPU, sample, and animated GPU
comparison limits unchanged. A retry that exhausts its remaining deadline now
reports the last completed mismatch instead of replacing its diagnostics with a
generic timeout. Raw-pixel inputs validate dimensions and buffer length before
pinning or native image creation.

The focused resolver/resource suite passes 53 tests, and the focused sample and
infrastructure suite passes 105. The unfiltered console solution passes 6,437
core tests with 23 skips, one singleton test, 50 gallery tests, four Vulkan
tests with 21 skips, and two Direct3D tests with three skips.

~~ Canonicalize references and capture diagnostics ~~

Place references at
`tests/Goldens/{Samples|Visual}/{profile}/[{maximum-version}/]{case}[.variant][.architecture].png`.
Move 82 visual and 37 existing non-Appium sample PNGs byte-for-byte into that
layout, then add the reviewed x64 macOS Blazor CPU reference carried from
#5421. The resulting inventory has 120 PNGs: 119 migrated references and one
additional architecture-specific reference.

GoldenAssets.targets gives copy and embedded-resource consumers the same stable
logical names. Successful resolved comparisons emit unversioned
`##SKIA-GOLDEN##` records so CI can retain captures and reviewers can promote
intentional updates. Proposal export deduplicates identical payloads, rejects
conflicting bytes for one key, and validates PNG structure, dimensions, safe
relative paths, containment, and symlink escapes.

Embedded-resource verification passes, and all eight exporter regression tests
pass. The design deliberately has no JSON catalog, schema migration inventory,
provider registry, compatibility layer, or Appium capture data.

~~ Stabilize browser sample capture and CI ~~

Playwright selects its bundled Chromium for the host hardware even when the
managed test process is translated. Use OSArchitecture for browser golden
identity while retaining ProcessArchitecture for managed host samples; changing
the global visual policy would incorrectly couple managed/native references to
browser selection. Add the reviewed x64 macOS reference with blob
5f93998ae75df547dc105e4144dc9e61f9d4217d for the translated-runner case.

Treat Playwright mirror messages on standard error as ordinary installer output,
while still failing a nonzero installer exit. Publish timestamped sample results
from `output/logs/testlogs/samples/**/*.trx`. Before taking the animated GPU
capture, require `.overlay-stats` to report a positive integer FPS; retain the
existing 6% mean RGBA comparison budget.

mismatch in #5421. Automatic public build 1647669 for this exact head passed
sample Build and Host jobs on Windows, Linux, and macOS, plus Docker jobs on
Windows and Linux. The remaining managed, native, package, and platform test
jobs also passed.

The shared test assembly uses modern C# syntax while still participating in

configuration into SkiaSharp.Build.targets for importing non-native projects on
net4*, netstandard2.0, and netstandard2.1. This keeps compiler support consistent
without adding a shipping package dependency.

5395.title: [tests] Extract shared Apple and Android device test infrastructure
5395.body:
[tests] Own mobile test devices and cover runtime bounds (#5395)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5373
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5391
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1641500
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3110270
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3110421

Make the existing DeviceRunners jobs own isolated simulators and emulators,
then exercise deliberate older and current runtime pairs without taking on the
Appium sample scenarios from #5373 and #5391. The shared lifecycle is consumed
by current device tests, so feature PRs can build on it without duplicating
process, identity, or cleanup policy.

~~ Consolidate test runner entry points ~~

Rename `test-shared.cake` to `tests-shared.cake`, move
`scripts/infra/samples/samples.cake` to
`scripts/infra/tests/tests-samples.cake`, and replace the combined
`tests-apple.cake` with single-purpose iOS and Mac Catalyst entry points. Keep
common test helpers and cache inputs beside the runners that consume them;
Mac Catalyst remains simulator-free and sample execution does not acquire
Appium setup.

Root and direct Cake target listings, YAML parsing, and public CI verified the
reorganized paths and target composition.

~~ Own Apple simulators by UUID ~~

The old iOS task deleted a timestamp name with `--force`, swallowed cleanup
errors, and did not retain ownership when creation succeeded but later setup
failed. Create a GUID-named simulator, validate JSON because the pinned Apple
tool can print failure text while returning zero, and record the returned UUID
before reading runtime metadata or booting it.

Pass that UUID to DeviceRunners and shutdown and delete only it during
teardown. Preserve the original setup or test exception while aggregating
cleanup failures. Resolve patch requests such as 26.3.1 through
CoreSimulator's major/minor runtime identifier, retain the exact returned
runtime version, and install an explicit older runtime only after verifying
the `simctl` inventory.

~~ Own Android emulators by process and identity ~~

The old runner reused `DEVICE_TESTS_EMULATOR`, relied on tool-managed startup,
and deleted the AVD without owning a serial or native process. Select an exact
installed system image and model, assign a GUID AVD and the first free even
console port from 5554 through 5682, start the SDK emulator directly, retain
its process and stdout/stderr logs, and bind DeviceRunners to
`emulator-{port}`. Physical-device selection retains its attached-device path
without creating an emulator.

Keep direct SDK lifecycle management because the pinned AndroidSdk.Tool 0.35.1
does not retain the emulator process and its wrappers can lose native exit
status needed for strict cleanup. Readiness requires the exact owned AVD name:
strip one terminal `OK` from the console response and consult
`ro.boot.qemu.avd_name` only when that response is blank, never to override a
nonblank mismatch. Give API 21 a 4 GiB userdata partition after its default
partition failed app installation with `INSTALL_FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE`.

On failure, retain diagnostics, terminate the owned process tree, wait for its
serial and ports to disappear, and delete the AVD only after process death.
Partial-create cleanup first confirms the exact owned name in the full AVD
inventory, and cleanup failures are aggregated with the original exception.

~~ Exercise older and current mobile runtimes ~~

Replace the single Android API 36 and iOS 26.2 jobs with API 21/API 36 and iOS
18.6/latest pairs. Keep each image or runtime beside its model in the stage
matrix, while retaining `ANDROID_PLATFORM_VERSIONS` for independent
compile-time `android.jar` provisioning.

API 21 is the declared Android minimum and predates Vulkan, so it skips
`ganesh-vulkan`, `graphite-vulkan`, and `ganesh-vulkan-sharpvk`; API 36 retains
the required Vulkan suite. An API 24 trial booted but failed all ten required
Vulkan tests, demonstrating why minimum-platform coverage and Vulkan coverage
use different runtime entries. iOS 18.6 supplies an explicit older-runtime
check, while `latest` exercises the newest installed runtime.

Public build 1641500 and package build 3110270 succeeded. Exact-package test
run 3110421 consumed the same source and package; its mobile jobs completed
with zero failures:

  * Android API 21: 1,269 total, 1,176 passed, 93 skipped.
  * Android API 36: 1,269 total, 1,186 passed, 83 skipped.
  * iOS 18.6: 1,251 total, 1,165 passed, 86 skipped.
  * iOS latest: 1,251 total, 1,165 passed, 86 skipped.

The first iOS 18.6 task exited after 733 tests with no test failures; the
existing task retry created a new owned simulator and completed the suite. The
overall test run was red for an unrelated Azure NuGet DNS failure in macOS
package tests and the known 0.630% macOS Blazor golden mismatch, not for its
mobile jobs.

~~ Preserve GPU policy in packaged hosts ~~

DeviceRunners prebuilds Android before emulator startup and later invokes the
suite with `noBuild`, so a GPU opt-out passed only to the test invocation cannot
change the packaged app. Pass `SkiaSharpTestSkipGpu` to that prebuild and emit
`SkiaSharp.Tests.SkipGpu` as both a runtime host option and assembly metadata,
because Android packaging did not preserve the runtime configuration value.

Resolve the policy from AppContext first, assembly metadata second, and the
environment last. The API 21 job's 93 skips versus API 36's 83 are the expected
ten-test delta from the three configured Vulkan backends; CPU, OpenGL, and UI
coverage remained required.

then threw TaskCanceledException because the shared HttpClient timeout

covering response headers and complete body buffering. Use the same
budget for readiness probes and functional requests rather than adding

redirects and proxies, and the single functional image request. Keep PNG,
dimension and golden-image checks unchanged rather than retrying a failed

before issuing the request.

5352.title: Bind bundled HarfBuzz functions locally on Linux
5352.body:
Bind bundled HarfBuzz functions locally on Linux (#5352)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3038
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/2247
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5366
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1637759
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1637595

Keep internal HarfBuzz calls within the bundled implementation and add a
native regression that demonstrates the failure without depending on GTK,
system HarfBuzz versions, fonts, or a managed-process crash.

~~ Prevent ELF preemption from mixing private HarfBuzz objects ~~

Using HarfBuzzSharp after GTK initialization can cause SIGSEGV or invalid
pointer errors. GTK can load system HarfBuzz into the global symbol scope;
ELF lookup can then redirect internal calls from libHarfBuzzSharp.so to
that implementation, passing private objects between incompatible builds.
Resolving the initial managed import from the intended library does not
control the native calls made inside it.

The earlier RTLD_DEEPBIND workaround lived in the custom library loader,
so it did not protect the .NET import path reported in this regression.
Apply -Wl,-Bsymbolic-functions in the common Linux HarfBuzz link recipe
instead, following the native-binding diagnosis in the issue discussion.

Choose function-only binding rather than -Bsymbolic: the observed conflict
is in function references, and the narrower option avoids extending the
change to global data binding. Keep the exported hb_* entry points and
managed signatures unchanged rather than introducing prefixed wrappers.
The nodeps and clang-cross recipes delegate to this common recipe and
inherit the option; other native recipes are not changed.

~~ Make load-order regression failures observable in native CI ~~

Add HarfBuzzSymbolBinding as a folder-discovered PowerShell case in the
SkiaSharp.Tests.Native project introduced by #5366. Separate the loader,
conflicting exports, and intentionally preemptible control into probe.c,
interposer.c, and control.c.

The loader obtains entry points from the explicit library handle and
exercises font creation and OpenType function initialization. Each probe
runs in a fresh native process, optionally loading the interposer with
RTLD_GLOBAL first. This keeps load-order state separate between probes
and prevents a native failure from terminating the xUnit host.

Have the interposer report the unexpectedly called function and exit 86,
rather than relying on incompatible object layouts to produce a segfault.
Require the fake control to pass alone and fail with that diagnostic and
exit code before trusting the produced-library checks. This rejects a
false pass caused by an inactive conflict.

Validate the exact linux and linuxnodeps artifact paths, ELF class,
endianness, machine, shared-library type, and glibc dependency before
execution. Exercise both variants alone and with the conflicting exports.
Declare a non-Linux runtime skip; unsupported Linux hosts, missing tools,
missing artifacts, and failed native commands remain failures. Remove
LD_PRELOAD and LD_AUDIT from the probe environment.

Use the existing xUnit execution, timeout, and TRX reporting rather than
adding another runner. Install gcc, glibc-devel, and binutils explicitly
in the Linux test image alongside LLVM; GCC also needs the assembler and
linker to compile these probes.

A Linux ARM64 before/after run used identical test sources and image,
substituting the standard HarfBuzz binary and its versioned alias. The
unfixed production binary from build 1637595 passed alone but called the
global hb_font_set_funcs_using with the interposer, producing exit 86:
12 native cases passed and this case failed. Restoring the fixed binary
from contributor build 1637759 produced 13 passes with no skips; its
nodeps HarfBuzz binary also passed both load orders.

Those runtime checks used production-built HarfBuzz libraries; the other
artifact inspections in that local run used retained fixtures. They do
not establish a full GTK application run or runtime coverage of musl,
Bionic, Tizen, or every cross-built architecture.

5378.title: Remove unused web assets and scope reviewed CodeQL findings
5378.body:
Remove unused web assets and scope reviewed CodeQL findings (#5378)

Context: https://github.com/google/angle/blob/ea1cea778c4a2312ef1b963b29a62fe595dd4df8/src/libANGLE/ProgramExecutable.cpp#L2986-L2995
Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/blob/7f0c3d39be96525be511614c28742e709a496dd9/src/core/SkDocument.cpp#L45-L68
Context: https://github.com/freetype/freetype/blob/0a0221a1347e2f1e07c395263540026e9a0aa7c7/src/raster/ftraster.c#L2520-L2524
Context: https://github.com/freetype/freetype/blob/37515cf56ba3349656049edbed89ffc6f6466f2d/src/raster/ftraster.c#L2749-L2755

Remove dependencies the web sample does not consume, and make vendor
analysis exceptions explicit rather than rewriting upstream contracts or
excluding whole dependency trees. Keep native runtime code, dependency
revisions and public APIs unchanged.

~~ Remove unused template dependencies without changing navigation ~~

Basic/Web loads jQuery 3.7.1 but its Razor pages and site.js have no jQuery
calls or validation consumers. Remove jquery, jquery-validation and
jquery-validation-unobtrusive, including their distributed variants and
maps, rather than editing vendor internals or hiding them behind another
delivery mechanism.

Remove the unused import-map tag, standalone bootstrap-grid.css,
bootstrap-reboot.css and bootstrap-utilities.css, RTL copies, and unused
unminified, non-bundle and ES-module JavaScript distributions.

Keep bootstrap.min.css, bootstrap.bundle.min.js, their maps and Bootstrap's
license. The full stylesheet provides the sample's grid/reboot/utility
styles, and Bootstrap 5 still owns its data-bs mobile-navigation
interaction without jQuery. Keep the otherwise-empty site.js as the
sample's extension point.

Local HTTP/browser checks exercised the images and mobile menu without
jQuery; the image API output matched its reference byte-for-byte.

~~ Keep result filtering narrower than source exclusion ~~

Add root CodeQL.yml with eleven entries covering twelve exact file/rule
pairs and fourteen reviewed locations. Use opaque rule IDs rather than
blanket third-party, test-directory or language exclusions. The filters
operate on reported results after analysis, not database extraction.
Keep the exceptions in the parent repository rather than editing files
that dependency synchronization would overwrite.

Separate Used runtime files from Unused upstream tools/tests. Each entry
records its reviewed file, lines, code and rationale. Those coordinates
are evidence, not line-scoped suppression: the file/rule pair also hides
future findings of that rule in that file. Re-review it when dependencies
or consumers change, and retain the required security/cryptography review.
Unused means outside supported SkiaSharp execution, not impossible to run
manually or harmless in an upstream workflow.

~~ Preserve upstream contracts outside supported execution ~~

Use the Unused group for eight upstream maintenance/test files outside
supported SkiaSharp execution. Product builds select library targets and
Python workflows scope their test discovery to repository-owned tests.
Do not confuse the scripts with the Brotli, HarfBuzz or SPIRV-Cross
libraries they accompany.

  * infra/bots/recipes/compile.py uses truncated MD5 for builder/configuration
    output-directory names. Changing the hash changes cache paths and recipe
    expectations.
  * tools/macsdk_dir.py reproduces Bazel's MD5 workspace-cache layout.
    SkiaSharp's Apple GN builds select SDKs through find_xcode_sysroot.py;
    changing this helper's algorithm would break its upstream lookup.
  * Brotli's scripts/dictionary/step-03-validate-bin.py reports MD5/SHA1
    dictionary diagnostics alongside SHA256. Preserve the expected digest
    formats rather than mechanically substituting another algorithm.
  * HarfBuzz's test/fuzzing/hb_fuzzing_tools.py names corpus seeds by SHA1;
    test/shape/run-tests.py fingerprints the font fixture version before
    shaping/output comparison. Neither is a product authentication decision.
  * SPIRV-Cross's test_shaders.py compares normalized generated output with
    regression references using MD5.
  * infra/bots/zip_utils_test.py deliberately uses broad modes, including
    0o777, to verify ZIP permission preservation under a private temporary
    root. Reducing the mask would weaken the fixture.
  * tools/run-wasm-gm-tests/run-wasm-gm-tests.js is an upstream CanvasKit/GM
    harness outside supported SkiaSharp flows. X-MD5-Hash labels image
    results, not credentials. Its HTML/file-write routes can still be unsafe
    if that server is run; the exclusion records execution scope, not safety.

~~ Bound the ANGLE sampler loop before counter wrap ~~

ProgramExecutable.cpp is used by WinUI's ANGLE graphics stack. In the
reviewed updateSamplerUniform implementation, an out-of-range starting
offset returns before subtraction, and safeUniformCount is clamped to the
remaining uint16_t textureUnitsCount.

The positive bound cannot exceed 65,535. The final executed iteration is
therefore at most 65,534; incrementing to 65,535 is representable and the
comparison then exits. Scope SM01928 to this file on that specific range
argument, not an assertion that other ANGLE loops or revisions are safe.

~~ Respect derived document finalization ~~

SkDocument.cpp backs the exposed PDF/XPS factories. The current PDF, XPS
and MultiPicture implementations call close() in their derived destructors,
as required by SkDocument.h, while virtual dispatch still reaches the
derived implementation.

close() finishes any active page and establishes closed state. The base
destructor's subsequent close() returns through that state without reaching
the reported onEndPage()/onClose() hooks again. Scope SM03728 to this
supported-subclass invariant; a future subclass violating the cleanup
contract needs renewed review.

~~ Record the FreeType language-semantics limitation ~~

ftraster.c is compiled into the selected FreeType renderer and can serve
monochrome glyphs. The reported (&buffer)[1] expression intends a
one-past-end address, but absence of a demonstrated buffer read is not a
complete proof of strict-C conformance.

Record SM01947 as an explicit vendor exception, not unused code or a
proven false positive. Both reviewed FreeType 2.14.3 and 2.15.0 sources
retain the expression, so that upgrade alone does not remove the report.
Canonical buffer-plus-count arithmetic remains preferable upstream, and
this file-wide rule exception must not stand in for rasterizer safety.

~~ Classify analysis metadata outside artifact dependency inputs ~~

The new root configuration otherwise fails repo-deps.py validate before
native build stages with:

  [FAIL] UNCOVERED FILES:
  CodeQL.yml

Classify CodeQL.yml in scripts/infra/caching/repo-deps.json's exclude list.
That list accounts for tracked files that are not artifact dependencies;
it is separate from CodeQL's source-result filters. Cache-key generation
continues to hash selected file contents and include submodule revisions.

The coverage validator passes, and the aggregate all-job cache-key output
is identical for the classification change alone. YAML parsing and scope
checks verify the grouping and exact selectors, not central alert
clearance.

5383.body:
Raise Apple deployment minimums (#5383)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/403
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/7f0c3d39be96525be511614c28742e709a496dd9...99f0073cf16d5baddce80621cbab3c0daa5609b0

Establish macOS 11.0 and iOS/tvOS/Mac Catalyst 14.0 as the native Apple
deployment baselines for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp. Express the policy
in native build defaults and managed support metadata without treating a
native library's minimum as permission to lower a consuming target's
existing higher requirement.

~~ Align native compilation and project defaults ~~

Cake previously selected macOS 10.13 on Intel and 11.0 on ARM64,
iOS/tvOS 11.0, and Mac Catalyst 13.1. The Xcode projects retained older
defaults, so direct project builds and Cake builds did not express the
same deployment policy.

Target macOS 11.0 on both architectures and iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst
14.0. Align Debug and Release settings in the SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp
Xcode projects with those values. Retain GetDeploymentTarget methods so
future platform or architecture differences can use the existing
selection boundary.

Advance externals/skia from 7f0c3d39be96 to 99f0073cf16d. The companion
changes the four corresponding GN defaults; compiler and linker flags
already consume those arguments. Keep the existing m156 engine, C API,
dependency pins, and watchOS configuration unchanged.

Xcode 27 rejected that deployment target, so validation used installed
Xcode 26.6 through DEVELOPER_DIR rather than raising the product floor
or changing the machine-wide Xcode selection. GN generation confirmed
the deployment flags for ARM64 and x64 across the four Apple targets;
generation alone is not target-platform runtime verification.

~~ Keep managed support metadata consistent with native requirements ~~

Shared iOS and tvOS metadata advertised 12.2, below the new native
requirement. Raise SupportedOSPlatformVersion and TargetPlatformMinVersion
together to 14.0 so those managed targets describe the required floor.

Retain managed macOS 12.0 and Mac Catalyst 15.0. Native and managed
minimums describe different layers; aligning the native baseline does
not justify lowering existing managed or application requirements.
Sample and device-test minimums remain unchanged, as do SDK and
target-framework versions.

changes. The local unfiltered console run encountered a typeface-stream

ARM64 reference at 1,832 of 65,536 pixels (2.7954%). The previous 2%
allowance admitted 1,310 outliers; 3% admits 1,966. PR #5183 selected the

byte-identical to CI, while Apple M3 Pro reproduces the failure. CI did

remains inferred rather than directly observed.

four-sample coverage atlas even though the output surface requests no
MSAA. The hardware and software sample patterns cover two versus three
samples along the diagonal edge, producing gray values of 127 versus 64.
The architecture-specific golden lookup is correct; CPU architecture
alone does not distinguish these rasterization profiles.

Absorb this measured variation through the shared GPU outlier budget
rather than raising channel tolerance or replacing the reference again.
This deliberately permits more over-tolerance pixels in GPU comparisons;
it does not distinguish expected edge differences from unrelated errors.
Renderer-specific references would provide finer discrimination.

5366.title: Add native artifact inspection tests and dedicated Linux CI
5366.body:
Add native artifact inspection tests and dedicated Linux CI (#5366)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/3038
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5352
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3106805
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1638964

Separate native artifact validation from artifact production. Inspect the
merged outputs with ordinary xUnit/TRX reporting instead of keeping those
assertions in native build jobs. Keep Package build-only, and report
compatibility and symbol failures through the test pipelines.

~~ Add a case without extending the runner ~~

Add SkiaSharp.Tests.Native and its dedicated solution. One xUnit theory
discovers Cases/Name.ps1 or Cases/Name/test.ps1, so a scenario can include
supporting files without C# registration or another test framework.
Share artifact layouts and inspection helpers through Helpers.psm1.

Supply the checkout root through the NativeTest.RepositoryDirectory
MSBuild runtime configuration value rather than walking parent folders.
Clear stale copied cases before building, then copy the current scripts
to the output directory so deleted tests cannot remain discoverable.

Run each case in a separate pwsh process, capture stdout/stderr, and kill
its process tree after five minutes. Missing entry points and unexpected
exit codes fail. Exit 77 requires an explicit SKIP reason; exceptions do
not become skips.

~~ Make uninspected additions to the native collection fail ~~

Fixed lists alone can silently omit newly added libraries or targets.
Compare the required inventory with files detected by suffix and binary
signature in output/native and output/msvc/native. Reject missing files,
duplicate claims, unclaimed binaries and entries without an inspection
case, including extensionless framework/DWARF files and newly bundled
binaries inside the Dawn package.

Consume native_msvc separately because its desktop MSVC outputs are not
included in the merged native artifact. Compare versioned ELF files and
retained libHarfBuzzSharp.wasm.a aliases with their normalized originals
by hash. Require the published Windows ARM64 paths directly rather than
searching alternate directory spellings.

~~ Preserve Linux dependency and minimum-runtime contracts ~~

Require fontconfig in normal glibc/musl Skia builds and exclude it from
nodeps and Bionic outputs. Inspect both libraries across the declared
architecture and variant combinations without loading target code.

Keep GLIBC ceilings directly in the compatibility test: 2.27 for x86,
x64 and arm64; 2.35 for arm; 2.39 for riscv64; and 2.42 for loongarch64.

installation, alternate-tool selection or fallback path searches.

against x86, x86_64, armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a directories. A library and
matching debug file copied into the wrong ABI directory must not pass
merely because their alignment and identities agree.

presence does not prove compiler mitigation, CFG or complete Spectre

WinUI, ANGLE and projection artifacts on the Linux host.

Require desktop Skia DLLs to delay-load D3D12 and D3DCompiler, with neither
present as a hard import. Exclude Nano Server from that requirement
because its native build disables Direct3D.

reject additional native entries.

Claim framework-root and Versions/Current aliases explicitly, including
directories materialized when pipeline artifacts dereference symlinks.

directories and hiding extra native files.

~~ Check the Tizen ABI without executing Tizen code ~~

Require x86_64/aarch64 ELF64 shared libraries and selected public SkiaSharp
or HarfBuzz exports. These checks catch incorrect architecture and missing
entry points without requiring a Tizen runtime; they do not establish
runtime behavior.

~~ Inspect every listed WebAssembly archive member ~~

Inspect both libraries for Emscripten 3.1.34, 3.1.56 and 6.0.2 across the
declared single-threaded, multithreaded and SIMD combinations. Require
nonempty archives, wasm32 WebAssembly headers for the listed members,
and selected defined public symbols. A valid archive container must not
hide an accidentally bundled host object.

~~ Separate build-only packaging from artifact test results ~~

Remove CheckLinuxDependencies, CheckWindowsDependencies, CheckAlignment
and Android build-ID/debuglink assertions from Cake, including callers
and obsolete verification arguments. Their responsibilities now live in
the inspection cases. Keep compilation, copying, stripping, symbol
extraction, debuglink creation and build-input/toolchain validation in
the producers.

Expose tests-native through Cake. Add a Linux native_tests leaf stage to
Test and Complete: Test depends on prepare and downloads source-build
artifacts; Complete depends on native artifact merging. Packaging does
not wait for native_tests, and Package does not include it. Keep tests on
standard templates without forwarding native-build 1ES settings.

Use a dedicated Azure Linux .NET SDK image with LLVM, leaving native
build images and minimal managed-runtime images unchanged. Publish TRX
and logs on failure; failed tests or missing result files fail the job.
The twelve current cases inspect target files without executing target
libraries or requiring a C compiler.

Internal run 3106805 passed twelve cases on each Linux/Windows host
against production Package build 3104558. Public Windows used a different
image whose LLVM tools were not on PATH. Keep that host invocation out
rather than hiding missing tools or restoring a defensive installer;
Windows DLL/PDB inspection still runs on Linux.

After rebasing onto main d29d6e6cd419, public run 1638964 passed all twelve

5361.body:
Stabilize browser sample captures and stable Uno startup (#5361)

Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1636281
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5353
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5293/checks?check_run_id=116262705576
Context: https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/pull/24260
Changes: https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/compare/f4d493c4034c3f49b5564a02f1eac5c044e834c7...da217df2312e9e39676880f9cb4b8d519cc297e0

Handle CSS transitions, eventual image readiness, and Uno splash dismissal
at their respective boundaries rather than relaxing golden comparisons.
Keep the Basic Uno sample on a stable SDK and retain repository mirrors
for dependency resolution.

~~ Finish CSS transitions before screenshot capture ~~

The Windows Blazor drawing test cleared its canvas correctly, but its
cleared-page screenshot differed by 1906 pixels inside the Clear button.
Its hover-exit background transition was still running after the canvas
readiness assertions had passed.

Set ScreenshotAnimations.Disabled in BrowserRunningApp.Screenshot so
Playwright finishes finite CSS transitions during capture. This does not
wait for WASM canvas painting. Retain the drawing pixel assertions and
existing comparison thresholds; no Blazor references change.

Verify the capture behavior with a transition paused halfway: the captured
100x100 swatch must contain its final color, not the intermediate color.

~~ Give eventual image readiness one bounded comparison loop ~~

A visible Blazor CPU canvas can precede its first raster presentation.
The pixel-readiness fix in #5353 addressed that gap, but separate pixel
and image checks give startup different readiness conditions and deadlines.

Add an opt-in SampleImage.Validate capture-delegate overload that returns
the matching image path. Retry dimension and pixel mismatches against the
reviewed reference, using the existing comparison options. Default to a
two-second budget with 100ms polling; the CPU startup test explicitly
allows ten seconds and returns on the first matching capture.

Replace BlazorWebAssemblyCpuSampleRuns(delayFirstPaint), its one-second
module-delay case, and its opaque-pixel probe with a normal startup test
using the complete golden image as its readiness condition. Do not apply
eventual matching globally to drawing or GPU assertions: a matching frame
does not establish that every intermediate frame was correct.

Limit each capture await to the remaining budget and test cancellation.
WaitAsync stops waiting; it does not cancel the underlying capture.
Propagate capture errors and cancellation rather than treating them as
image mismatches. Missing references and corrupt images also fail without
retrying. Preserve one-shot validation and produce the usual diagnostics
when a completed mismatch persists until the deadline.

Exercise transient and persistent mismatches, dimension changes, retained
diagnostics, invalid deadlines, stalled captures, and error propagation.
A browser test captures an incorrect frame followed by the expected frame;
the console-error test verifies browser errors still escape through the
capture loop.

~~ Adopt stable Uno without accepting unrelated image changes ~~

Update the Basic Uno sample from Uno.Sdk 6.6.0-dev.208 to stable 6.7.30,
which selects runtime 6.7.135. Keep repository package sources unchanged:
the required dependencies are supplied through the existing mirrors.
Add a contract test for the artifacts, dotnet-public, and dotnet-eng
source/mapping keys; generated SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp consumers
remain restricted to staged artifacts.

The newer navigation template changes top-navigation spacing. Review and
update the nine Uno references for that layout change: 1556 CPU navigation
pixels and 1582 Drawing navigation pixels per reference. Every pixel below
the 49-pixel navigation header remains unchanged, including scene content,
strokes, the Clear button, and drawing controls. Stable CPU and drawing
tests pass these references without changing their tolerances.

~~ Keep recording until Uno dismisses its startup splash ~~

The Windows Uno failure remained on .uno-loader until startup timed out.
Reproduce the symptom locally on stable 6.7.30 with 4x Chromium CPU
throttling: the loader stays visible for 60 seconds despite an existing
canvas and no browser errors.

Uno subscribes to CompositionTarget.FrameRendered, then requests a
presentation through IXamlRootHost.InvalidateRender. Presentation can
reuse an existing recording without raising the event needed to remove
the splash. The upstream correction requests a new recorded frame, but
that correction is absent from the selected stable runtime.

Add a WebAssembly-only partial App hook before window activation.
Temporarily subscribe to the public CompositionTarget.Rendering event,
whose stable implementation requests recorded frames. Let Uno remove
its own loader, then unsubscribe. Also stop on window close. An
independent non-repeating 60-second dispatcher timer unsubscribes and
reports an explicit error if dismissal never completes. Do not hide the
loader or substitute screenshot retries for application recovery.

The workaround passed 32 local cold starts, including 20 consecutive
4x-throttled starts. Observation confirmed cleanup after natural dismissal.
A fault-injected observer that never reported dismissal triggered the
timeout error and stopped observing. These checks support the workaround,
not a guarantee over every scheduling interleaving.

Retain the existing normal Uno startup, rendering, navigation, drawing,
and clear tests without permanent loader-query instrumentation. Remove
the workaround when the sample adopts a runtime containing the upstream
recorded-frame correction.

The final head passes the Windows, Linux, and macOS sample Host and Build
checks and both sample Docker checks.

Make Skia sync validation fail reliably and retain attempt evidence (#5379)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5371
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/38813366901

Give the update agent focused validation commands whose process results
and retained artifacts can be checked independently of its summary. The
m157 investigation exposed shell pipelines that could mask command
failures, while publishing required only a successful test exit record.

~~ Preserve the actual command result ~~

Add build_native.py, build_managed.py and run_tests.py. Each script runs
its canonical commands through shared subprocess handling without a shell
pipeline, captures combined stdout/stderr, records the exit code and
returns failure to its caller. Native tool restore must succeed before
Cake starts; executable-launch failures and child termination are also
recorded as failures.

Keep platform and architecture selection in Cake. The native wrapper
requires explicit values but forwards them without an allowlist, so the
skill's example targets do not become an accidental support restriction.
The test helper retains the unfiltered net10.0 console solution command.

Support optional repository and artifact paths for local invocation.
Automation supplies the product checkout explicitly because its immutable
skill copy lives outside that checkout.

~~ Invalidate stale results and preserve attempts ~~

Before launching validation, remove that stage's exit record and those
of downstream stages. A native rerun invalidates native, managed and test
results; a managed rerun invalidates managed and test results. An
interrupted run therefore cannot leave its previous success record usable.

Archive an existing stage log before replacing it. Completed logs include
their exit code, preserving the outcome of failed attempts after a later
successful rerun overwrites the canonical exit record. The helpers do not
retry automatically.

This is evidence bookkeeping, not source-change detection: the agent must
still rebuild and retest when the validated source or native binary changes.

~~ Gate publishing on build and test evidence ~~

Require nonempty native, managed and test logs and an exit record containing
0 for each before the publishing script reaches Git or GitHub operations.
Previously, only the final test exit record was checked.

Update the skill's executable commands and handoff artifact list. Keep its
instructions focused on agent actions and failure gates, including explicit
handling of expected nonzero shell results instead of masking failures
through head or tee.
