5345.title: Synchronize Android texture rendering with display refresh
5345.body:
Synchronize Android texture rendering with display refresh (#5345)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/533
Context: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/Choreographer
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1633130

Drive automatic Android texture frames from the display clock instead of
buffer-swap throughput. Keep drawing on the existing GL worker and preserve
explicit render requests and synchronous lifecycle progress. The shared
GLTextureView base also covers MAUI Android SKGLView.HasRenderLoop without
changing its handler, public signatures, or native code.

~~ Bound automatic redraws without blocking explicit work ~~

Once its pause, surface, and size checks passed, IsReadyToDraw accepted
requestRender || renderMode == Rendermode.Continuously. Consuming the
explicit request therefore left the next continuous draw ready immediately,
and texture-backed swaps did not reliably throttle it to the display rate.
The API 24 baseline regression produced 980 paint callbacks during 46
display callbacks.

Obtain Choreographer through a main-Looper Handler and use its one-shot
callbacks to set frameRenderRequested and wake GLThread. Consume that
boolean when drawing starts so missed display pulses coalesce into one
pending automatic frame rather than a replay queue. Do not use a fixed
60 Hz timer or move GL rendering onto the UI thread.

  * Keep requestRender independent of the display-driven flag. Explicit
    requests and surface creation, resize, and resume must make progress
    while the UI thread may be synchronously waiting for the GL worker;
    requiring a callback on that blocked UI thread would stall progress.
  * Separate CanDraw from pending-frame demand. IsAbleToDraw uses drawable
    EGL state, while IsReadyToDraw additionally requires a render request,
    preserving the resize completion wait after a request is consumed.
  * Stop automatic callbacks for explicit pause, dirty mode, an unavailable
    or invalid surface, nonpositive dimensions, and worker exit. Clear
    pending automatic work and remove/dispose callback peers on the main
    Looper; worker-finally cleanup also schedules removal after an error.

Document that this paces automatic continuous rendering, not every possible
RequestRender call or the eventual presentation time of a frame. Preserve
request-driven WhenDirty rendering and queued GL-thread events.

Pacing assertions require nonzero painting and compare paint counts with
observed Choreographer callbacks, allowing two boundary frames rather than
assuming 60 FPS. A separate assertion checks painting stays off the UI
thread. Coverage also includes native requests, MAUI invalidation, mode
changes, a blocked worker, pause/resume, resize, and reattachment with both
render modes. The five tests pass on ARM64 Android API 24 and API 37
emulators. Current-source sampling averages approximately 60 FPS on their
60 Hz displays; physical and high-refresh displays were not validated, and
the counter assertions are not pixel or presentation tests.

~~ Keep callback lifetime separate from scheduling ~~

A FrameCallback instance does not prove its one-shot callback is pending.
A worker can select WhenDirty, let the scheduled DoFrame consume itself
without reposting, and restore Continuously before the queued Handler
update runs. Checking only for a non-null callback would then leave the
continuous render loop stopped.

Track frameCallbackPosted under the worker monitor. Clear it when the
matching callback starts and set it when posting. Rearm an existing object
when ShouldScheduleFrameCallback holds but nothing is posted. Reject a
stale callback identity before changing the current callback's posted state.

The regression orders GL-thread mode changes around the view's display
callback before queued Handler updates execute, then requires rendering
to resume within the display-paced bound. It reproduces zero subsequent
frames without the posted-state distinction and passes with this guard.

5312.title: Run generated browser samples with Playwright
5312.body:
Run generated browser samples with Playwright (#5312)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5308
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5291
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1633875

Validate package-consuming sample applications through their actual browser
UIs while keeping the test runner backed by repository source. Extend the
generated-sample foundation with browser interactions, reviewed screenshots
and explicit execution lifetimes rather than synthetic rendering apps.

Carry forward the browser slice of #5291 above the merged #5308 foundation.
Keep HTTP image checks independent of browser page checks, and retain the
separate Integration/MSBuild suites and their existing references.

~~ Exercise the generated applications, not substitute scenes ~~

Add named runtime facts for Basic Web, BrowserWebAssembly, Blazor CPU/GPU
and Drawing, and Uno CPU/Drawing. Build and launch generated copies against
the staged producing package cohort; the runner retains its SkiaSharp
ProjectReference and native import.

Add BrowserWebAssembly's native-assets project reference so generation also
supplies its SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.WebAssembly package dependency. Extend
the artifact-contract theory to check that generated reference.

Blazor Drawing selects colors and brush size, creates pointer strokes,
checks their pixels and clears them. Uno selects its declared
net10.0-browserwasm project target, waits beyond the splash screen, exercises
Drawing navigation and strokes, clears the canvas and returns to CPU
rendering. Its readiness check requires the rendered blue/purple scene,
not merely an existing canvas.

~~ Own browser lifetime and retain errors across operations ~~

BrowserRunningApp wraps the existing RunningApp rather than introducing
another server lifecycle. Callback completion disposes the browser context
and Chromium; the enclosing host callback retains process cleanup and logs.

Reuse the host's cached address and same-origin request validation for
browser navigation. Recognize BrowserWASM's "App url:" output alongside
"Now listening on:", accepting HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a nonzero port.

Collect console errors and page exceptions across the callback. Assert
after navigation, element waits, screenshots and callback completion so
errors between operations or direct Page interactions cannot disappear.
Sentinel regressions verify multiple console errors and asynchronous page
exceptions. Retain a failure screenshot when execution fails before its
first normal capture.

~~ Distinguish stable pixel goldens from animated GPU smoke checks ~~

Capture full pages with a 1280x900 viewport, device scale 1 and light color
scheme. Add nine reviewed page references for each of Linux, macOS and
Windows, including drawn and cleared states.

Consolidate ValidateFile, SaveAndValidate and CompareGolden into file and
byte-array SampleImage.Validate overloads with SampleImageOptions. Save
supplied bytes before checking the PNG signature, then compare dimensions
and pixels. ExpectedSize preserves fixed-size HTTP and Console assertions;
omitted options retain the 0.075% differing-pixel budget with zero channel
tolerance. Missing references fail without creating replacements.

The animated Blazor GPU page instead uses a 6% mean absolute RGBA error,
normalized by pixel count, four channels and 255. This replaces, rather than
supplements, the differing-pixel criterion. It is a coarse smoke check:
uniform dark output can pass, and arbitrary animation frames are not strict
rendering goldens. Do not freeze the sample clock or infer deterministic
frame equivalence from this result.

Regression tests cover explicit pixel budgets, alpha-inclusive mean error,
the exact 6% boundary and rejection one channel step beyond the boundary.

~~ Preserve diagnostic snapshots instead of masking image failures ~~

Actual and expected captures can share a basename, and a capture may be
attached more than once. Duplicate xUnit attachment names could obscure the
real pixel mismatch with an attachment exception.

Give expected images an expected- prefix and assign repeated names numeric
suffixes in SampleArtifacts. Keep actual, expected and diff evidence
distinct while retaining the existing 8 MiB embedding limit and on-disk
artifacts. Regressions exercise same-basename mismatches and repeated
diagnostic snapshots.

~~ Select declared frameworks without retargeting dependencies ~~

Use one optional DotNetOptions record across BuildSample, DotNet.Build and
callback-based DotNet.Run; name raw command execution Execute. Options cover
configuration, framework, additional properties, working directory and
timeout, with Release remaining the sample default.

Pass framework selection through --framework rather than overriding
TargetFramework or TargetFrameworks. Protect configuration and helper-owned
restore properties from additional-property overrides. A compiling
regression selects net10.0-windows while referenced projects retain their
netstandard2.1 and net10.0 targets.

Keep inherited PATH selection and private consumer caches. Preserve
30-minute build and one-minute raw-command defaults. A run timeout controls
address and exit waits, not callback duration or browser-operation waits;
cleanup and output reads retain their one-minute bounds. Tests cover
property forwarding, working directories, argument boundaries, invalid
options and cleanup after timed-out waits.

~~ Make build coverage and runtime coverage independently visible ~~

Combine the former BasicSampleTests and GallerySampleTests compilation
theories in SampleBuildTests. Retain Console and HTTP execution in
BasicSampleRunTests, put ordinary browser execution in BrowserSampleRunTests
and isolate Uno's framework-specific startup in UnoBrowserSampleRunTests.

Split DockerSampleTests into DockerSampleBuildTests and
DockerSampleRunTests. Both retain the Docker execution group: an image build
requires a daemon even though it is compilation coverage. Browser facts and
browser-error regressions use Host; infrastructure and generated compilation
remain Build. Discovery regressions check eligible Basic/Gallery cases and
the shared Docker fixture.

~~ Separate sample preparation from Docker resource ownership ~~

Replace Utils/SampleTestBase with root-level DotNetSampleTestBase and add
DockerSampleTestBase beside the test classes. The .NET base owns its prepared
workspace; the Docker base stages a flat selected-sample context, local
packages and relative NuGet feed, then deletes that context after building.

Do not impose common inheritance on these different workspace lifetimes.
Reuse SampleWorkspace.CopyTree instead. Context tests check selected inputs,
excluded bin/obj directories, package staging and an empty-cohort failure.

DockerSampleFixture retains daemon policy, cached images, registered tags,
container callbacks and resource cleanup. Register a tag before its build
and cache it after success. Share the fixture across Docker build/run classes
so the split does not create independent image caches.

Put CLI syntax and command bounds behind named Docker operations such as
Ps, Build, Run, Port, Wait and Logs. Fixture and running-app code call those
operations rather than constructing argument arrays.

~~ Serialize shared resources without blocking unrelated collections ~~

Remove AssemblyInfo.cs's assembly-wide DisableTestParallelization setting.
BrowserSampleRunTests and UnoBrowserSampleRunTests share one serial browser
collection; Docker build/run classes share another for their mutable image
cache and resource registry.

Neither collection sets DisableParallelization=true, so unrelated collections
can run concurrently. Normal xUnit serialization within a class or collection
still applies, including SampleBuildTests theory rows. A reflection regression
checks the assembly policy, browser assignments and nonexclusive collection
definitions.

~~ Install the matching browser at the CI execution boundary ~~

Add Microsoft.Playwright 1.55.0 and a CI-only pre-test Chromium installation
target. Pass SampleRunGroup from Cake so Host and unfiltered runs install
Chromium, while Build and Docker groups do not. Keep local installation an
explicit documented prerequisite rather than a fixture or discovery download.

Preserve the canonical eight Samples jobs and existing provisioning. Build
1633875 succeeded for source ffb7ec0adddf92e3b46c77fbeb2ec34146aed7cd through
merge 97bfa399c27477d894ace68ddd2df8ae706f4808.

Samples results were Linux Build 134, Host 14 and Docker 4; macOS Build 140
and Host 14; Windows Build 141, Host 14 and Docker 4. Those completed groups
reported zero failures and skips. Windows Host passed on its second attempt
without a source change after WebSampleReturnsImage exceeded the existing
four-second HTTP timeout. This records a successful retry, not a timeout fix
or proof that the failure cannot recur.

5339.title: Partition Samples CI by typed execution target
5339.body:
Partition Samples CI by typed execution target (#5339)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5314
Context: 8f25d525d2ed42a9e73d5d5fb78c2af93f53e818
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1632894

Separate sample compilation, host application execution and container
execution through a fixed execution-target contract. Keep grouping independent
of consumer SDK selection, preserve full local runs, and report CI partitions
without changing the existing toolchains or producing package cohorts.

~~ Require one typed execution group for Samples tests ~~

Add SampleRunGroup and RunGroupAttribute, emitting the standard xUnit
RunGroup trait. Build covers generated Basic/Gallery compilation and
infrastructure checks; Host covers Console/Web execution; Docker covers the
container fixture. Android, Ios, Mac and Windows reserve native execution
targets rather than naming sample families.

Use class annotations for homogeneous fixtures and method annotations for
the mixed Basic tests. A Samples-only Roslyn analyzer reports missing,
multiple or undefined effective groups and rejects raw Xunit.TraitAttribute
RunGroup declarations as errors SKS001 through SKS004.

Detect Fact/Theory and derived attributes semantically. Include inherited,
overridden and default-interface test methods, respecting AttributeUsage
separately along the method and class inheritance chains. Otherwise a
discovered test could bypass the annotation requirement and disappear from
filtered CI. This validates group annotations, not CI routing or dynamically
generated case completeness.

Keep the analyzer on netstandard2.0 when solution-wide net10.0 framework
properties are supplied, and reference it as an analyzer rather than a
runtime dependency. Preserve the runner's source-backed project references.

~~ Keep filtering opt-in at the shared runner boundary ~~

Add case-sensitive --runGroup selection through the standard
--filter-trait RunGroup=<group> argument. An omitted selector passes no filter
and keeps the full local suite; unknown groups fail with ArgumentException
instead of silently selecting no tests.

Extend RunDotNetTest with optional runnerArguments, quoting and appending them
after its existing report and hang-dump arguments. The .NET Core, container
and MSBuild callers do not acquire Samples filters or changed defaults.
Retain Samples' existing no-build selection and disabled activity hang monitor.

Accept sampleRunId only with ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
Place results below that run ID and the timestamp so CI partitions have
separate TRX locations without changing the default local results layout.

~~ Split CI only across supported execution targets ~~

Replace the three monolithic Samples host jobs with a shared Samples job
template: Windows and Linux run Build, Host and Docker; macOS runs Build and
Host, producing eight jobs. macOS CI does not provision Docker; unfiltered
local runs retain the existing Docker availability behavior. Reserved native
groups do not create empty device jobs.

Retain the repository SDK, workload/Tizen settings, agents, platform setup,
native/NuGet acquisition and Docker image SDK pins. Give each OS/group a
distinct job name, result directory, TRX title and log artifact. Set Samples
execution retries to zero without changing provisioning or download retries.

Current-head Azure expansion at aaa3a4f99596 against main 888e7b3f7194 verifies
the eight-job matrix and unchanged non-Samples stages. Build 1632894 passed
the eight Samples partitions and the remaining stages at cf92d81522b2,
through merge 1afc8560b127. That full run predates the base update; it is not
exact-head CI proof for aaa3a4f99596.

~~ Retain diagnostics without republishing successful inputs ~~

The Windows job inherited successful whole-output publication and deleted
only downloaded NuGet packages before upload, leaving native inputs behind.
Set shouldPublish to false for every Samples job and remove the Windows-only
NuGet deletion step, which no longer serves a successful whole-output upload.

Declare output/logs through the shared publishArtifacts mechanism with
always: true for success/failure retention, replacing direct artifact tasks.
Keep PublishTestResults under always() and retain build/runner diagnostics
alongside test evidence. The shared failed-run whole-output snapshot remains
enabled; this change does not promise that failed uploads omit input cohorts.

5341.title: Share CI test-job setup through caller-configured templates
5341.body:
Share CI test-job setup through caller-configured templates (#5341)

Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1632922

Reduce repeated test-job setup and result publication without hiding each
runner's configuration inside platform switches. Keep stage composition
explicit and derive reporting names where the existing job identity already
provides the necessary information.

~~ Share execution setup while callers own the differences ~~

The Tests stage repeated SDK setup, native-artifact requirements and result
publication across its desktop, container and device/WASM jobs. Extract those
common bodies from azure-templates-stages-test.yml into three reusable job
templates, each invoking the existing bootstrapper once.

Pass job names, agents, arguments, environment, packages and pre-build steps
from the stage. Container callers supply image and native-platform values;
device callers supply SDK overrides and provisioning settings. This removes
duplication rather than merely relocating job bodies or introducing internal
runtime/platform switches.

Preserve the differences that describe the actual execution environments:

  * Android retains its dedicated agent and emulator/KVM provisioning.
  * Windows .NET Framework x86 retains its Vulkan opt-out because
    SwiftShader's LLVM JIT cannot resolve __chkstk in a 32-bit process.
    Windows provisioning and Linux software-GPU setup remain caller-owned.
  * Apple Metal and headless WASM WebGPU declarations retain their rationale.
    Containers share their no-GPU-stack declaration and install no host SDK.
  * Stable WASM retains Emscripten setup and visual-image extraction; preview
    WASM retains its explicit SDK selection and omits that extraction.

Keep prepare/native stage dependencies and coverage collection in the stage.
Leave the bootstrapper, outer pipeline gating and managed/MSBuild/Samples
jobs unchanged. Update the container and GPU-policy documentation to identify
the shared templates and caller-owned declarations.

~~ Derive reporting names without breaking artifact consumers ~~

Derive test-run titles as displayName followed by " Tests". The 15 test-job
display names are unique, so callers no longer repeat a separate title.
Ten displayed titles change, including removal of Android/iOS version
suffixes; versions remain in execution arguments and log artifact names.

Derive desktop log names by replacing tests_ with testlogs_, and coverage
names by replacing tests_ with coverage_. Core callers pass publishCoverage
rather than spelling out coverage artifact names. Preserve the existing
coverage_netcore_windows, coverage_netcore_macos and coverage_netcore_linux
names, matching coverage_reports dependencies and downloads. Publication
remains rooted at output/coverage, with reports read from
output/**/Cobertura.xml.

Actual Azure expansion at head 9c5fd64d76f versus main d41f3583b8b matches
the 12-stage, 92-job pipeline except the exact display-derived title changes.
Publisher/collector checks also verify the coverage links and the 15 unique
log artifacts, including their success/failure publication conditions.

Tests-stage runner jobs and Coverage Reports job completed successfully;
this evidence does not claim that the remaining pipeline stages passed.
